title: Monthly Invoice Run — ledger to numbered, recorded invoices
objective: Measure whether the invoice-run craftbook turns a seeded client roster and work ledger into one print-ready invoice per billable client with unbroken numbering, ledger-true amounts, and a run summary — numeric integrity is the class bar.
prompt: end of month — can you run the invoicing? three clients have billable work logged, last invoice number was 2026-041, dont break the sequnce

setup.about: Freelance office for Fieldnote Studio, a one-person design practice. The client roster is workspace/clients.json and the work ledger is workspace/ledger.json; invoices go under workspace/invoices.
setup.missionObjectives: Invoice amounts come from the tracked ledger only, numbering continues without a skip or repeat, and the books record what went out. No live services, no real credentials.

success.summary: invoices/ holds a print-ready invoice per billable client plus a run sheet whose numbers continue 2026-041 and whose amounts are ledger-true; report.md summarizes the run.

checks.label: the skipped client is named, not silently dropped

facts.label: Harbor & Pine amount from the ledger

axes.name: numeric integrity
axes.description: Every amount traces to a tracked ledger entry; nothing estimated or invented.

axes.name: numbering continuity
axes.description: Invoice numbers continue 2026-041 with no skip and no repeat.

axes.name: professionalism
axes.description: The invoices look worth paying — clear line items, terms-correct due dates, print-ready pages.

axes.name: completeness
axes.description: One invoice per billable client, the idle client skipped on purpose, and the books updated.

axes.name: print-polish
axes.description: Each invoice is styled for paper — an @page rule, honest margins, a professional face.
